summary: Unexpected 5xx delta after large embedding upload: GPU driver soft-reset correlated with apigw overload
customer_impact_summary: Customer Nimbus experienced elevated error rates (5xx) on their dedicated cluster during a large embedding upload that impacted production payment risk scoring. Approximately 8-12% of requests returned 5xx between 10:12–10:56 UTC, causing timeouts and failed batched scoring jobs.
description:
Issue summary:
Nimbus Financial reported a sudden rise in 5xx responses for their dedicated deployment while performing a large embedding upload and concurrent chat/embedding traffic. The wave began ~2026-03-10 10:12 UTC and subsided after 10:56 UTC.

Impact:
- Enterprise customer production latency and error budget hit; some scoring pipelines failed and were retried by the customer's orchestrator.
- Customer reported degraded UX for internal dashboards tied to inference results.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster (tenant: nimbus-prod) in us-east-1
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.3
- GPU image: rwinf/dedicated-gpu:2026-02-12 (NVML v460-driver)
- API gateway cluster version: apigw-3.1.1

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Customer uploaded a ~1.8M-vector embedding batch (multipart upload) at 10:10 UTC.
2) Simultaneous live chat traffic persisted to the same tenant (~120 concurrent streams).
3) Within ~2 minutes, apigw accept queue length increased and 502/503 responses started to spike.
4) Multiple serving runtime replicas reported NVML soft-resets and then restarts; apigw observed upstream resets and returned 502s.

Observed behavior:
- Apigw 502/503/504 spike correlated with GPU driver soft-reset spikes in telemetry.
- Keepalive counts dropped for upstream runtime sockets; accept queue grew.
- Prefetch cancellations and embedding shard rebalancer ran while the driver reset sequence occurred, leading to increased downstream retries and backpressure.

Expected behavior:
- Large embedding uploads should be rate-limited and isolated by the scheduler to avoid cascading soft-resets on shared GPUs. Runtime restarts should not cause sustained apigw 5xx floors.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- We advised the customer to stagger their large embedding upload and reduce chunk concurrency.
- Support temporarily pinned their tenant to a separate dedicated GPU pool while investigation proceeds.

investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Asha): correlated apigw 5xx spike with NVML soft-reset bursts across three runtime pods. Dashboard (grafana/embed-prod) shows NVML reset rate jumped at 10:13.
SRE (Diego): observed accept_queue growth on apigw and half-open upstream sockets; apigw timed out on hedged requests, amplified by client's retry logic.
Runtime team: driver logs show a pattern consistent with a long-running NVMe GC on host combined with a GPU watchdog throttle triggering soft-resets during heavy NVMe IO. Embedding upload triggered heavy NVMe writes for checkpointing embedding shards, which coincided with GPU driver scheduling delays.
Scheduler team: the dedicated scheduler allowed high multipart concurrency (default burst=20) for this tenant; this allowed many simultaneous GPU-intensive shard writes causing IO and GPU contention.
Hypothesis: a combined IO/GPU contention window caused NVML soft-resets; the restarts reduced available upstream capacity which pushed apigw into accept-queue saturation and 5xx responses. Hedged retries and the customer's upload concurrency amplified the backpressure.
Evidence: NVML reset timestamps align within 10s of apigw 502 spikes; NVMe iowait metrics increased ~5x during the window.
Next diagnostic steps: capture full runtime nvml logs, collect host dmesg, and reproduce with controlled embedding-burst in staging with same image and scheduler settings.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:05 - Diego Morales: Confirmed NVML soft-reset spikes across 3 replicas; opened INT ticket INT-883 to capture host-level kernel logs and NVMe stats.
2026-03-10 12:22 - Samantha Kim (Customer Success): Nimbus accepted temporary pin to separate GPU pool; they reported immediate reduction in 5xx. Customer requested root cause and mitigation plan.

2026-03-11 09:18 - Priya Nair (Runtime): Reproduced partial behavior in staging when running multipart embed upload + concurrent chat load; NVMe iowait increased and NVML reset observed after ~90s. Collecting strace + nvml traces.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-11):
- Temporarily moved Nimbus to isolated dedicated pool to restore production traffic.
- Reduced default multipart upload concurrency for dedicated scheduler to 6 for customers with >1TB shard activity.
- Released runtime image patch v2026.02.4 that adds guarded NVML watchdog backoff and better checkpoint IO yielding.
- Configured apigw to increase upstream keepalive timeout and reduce immediate hedged retry for affected tenant.

Status: Partial fix deployed (driver/ runtime patch + scheduler conservative defaults). Full RCA pending after host-level logs analyzed and NVMe mitigation validated. Follow-up owner: Priya Nair.
follow_up_actions: Backport runtime patch v2026.02.4 to all dedicated GPU images (owner: Priya Nair)
Add alert: NVML_soft_reset_rate > 3/min for any tenant -> paging SRE (owner: Diego Morales)
Audit scheduler burst defaults for dedicated clusters and create a safer default policy (owner: Scheduler team)
Run controlled embedding-burst test in staging with NVMe IO profiling and document threshold (owner: Runtime + Perf)
Confluence: write postmortem and guidance for customers on safe large-embedding uploads (owner: Customer Success)
Follow up with Nimbus on billing credits and confirmation their pipelines are healthy (owner: Samantha Kim)
